fact: 为减少对游客的干扰，霍华德·卡特与埃及工人于1922年11月1日开工，比往常的发掘季更早。11月4日，一名工人发现岩石中的一级台阶，该台阶被确认为一座陵墓入口楼梯的开端。按卡特发表的记述，工人是在拆除工棚遗迹下方挖掘时发现台阶；另有说法把发现归给一名在划定作业区外挖掘的男孩。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
sources.quote: To minimise the disruption to tourists, Carter and his Egyptian workforce began on 1 November 1922, earlier in the season than usual. ... On 4 November a worker uncovered a step in the rock. ... According to Carter's published account the workmen discovered the step while digging beneath the remains of the huts; other accounts attribute the discovery to a boy digging outside the assigned work area. The step proved to be the beginning of a tomb entrance staircase.

fact: 1922年11月23日以后，卡那封勋爵带女儿抵达卢克索，发掘继续。封门上的封印刻有图坦卡蒙的名字，提示这是他的陵墓；封门曾被部分拆毁后重新封闭，说明古代曾遭盗掘。11月26日发掘者抵达第二道封门。卡特在左上角凿开一个小孔，看到「黑暗与空无」，随即回答卡那封的询问——最著名的版本是「是的，了不起的东西」，但各种记述对原话并不一致。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
sources.quote: The digging resumed after 23 November with Carnarvon's arrival in Luxor with his daughter Lady Evelyn Herbert. ... Upon closer examination the doorway seal was found to be inscribed with the name of Tutankhamun, suggesting that this was his tomb. ... On 26 November the excavators reached another sealed doorway. With trembling hands I made a tiny breach in the upper left-hand corner. ... Carnarvon asked Carter if he could see anything. Accounts differ as to the wording of Carter's answer; in the best-known version, in his book, Carter replied "Yes, wonderful things."

fact: 1922年以前，埃及的新发掘高度依赖「分成制」（partage，又称文物分配制）：博物馆或私人收藏家出资赞助考古发掘，换取出土文物的一份，惯例为一半，其余归文物局及其博物馆（开罗埃及博物馆）。1922年，文物局局长拉科宣布终止给发掘者的传统「半份」：政府可以把文物作为礼物授予赞助人，但埃及境内一切文物在原则上属于政府。这一变更不适用于卡那封既有的特许权——该特许权允许分配文物，但完整未被盗的陵墓除外，其全部内容必须交给文物局。卡那封因此计划主张图坦卡蒙墓因古代被盗而不算「完整」，尽管它在古代曾被修复并重新封闭。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
sources.quote: New excavations of ancient sites were heavily dependent on the system known as 'partage' or 'division of finds': museums or private collectors of ancient artefacts would fund an Egyptological dig in exchange for a share of the artefacts, customarily half, and the remainder went to the Antiquities Service and its museum, the Egyptian Museum in Cairo. In 1922, Lacau had declared the end of the traditional half-share given to excavators; the government might grant artefacts to the sponsors of an excavation as gifts, but all antiquities in Egypt belonged in principle to the government. This change did not apply to Carnarvon's existing concession, which allowed for a division of finds except in case of an intact tomb, whose contents must be surrendered entirely to the Antiquities Service. Carnarvon had planned to argue that Tutankhamun's tomb did not qualify as intact because it had been robbed, even though it was restored and resealed in ancient times.

fact: 1922年2月28日，英国单方面宣布终止对埃及的保护权、承认埃及为独立主权国家，结束自1882年起的占领（共40年）。但宣言把四项事务「绝对保留」给英国政府裁量：英帝国在埃及的通讯安全、埃及的对外防御、埃及境内外国利益与少数群体的保护、苏丹。宣言同时规定，埃及政府须通过一项适用于境内全体居民的大赦法，1914年11月2日宣布的戒严才会撤销。历史学者埃尔金斯认为，这次独立并未带来主权，而是「半自治」地位。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence
sources.quote: The following principles are hereby declared: 1. The British Protectorate over Egypt is terminated, and Egypt is declared to be an independent sovereign State. 2. So soon as the Government of His Highness shall pass an Act of Indemnity with application to all inhabitants of Egypt, martial law as proclaimed on 2 November 1914, shall be withdrawn. 3. The following matters are absolutely reserved to the discretion of His Majesty's Government ... (a) The security of the communications of the British Empire in Egypt; (b) The defence of Egypt against all foreign aggression or interference, direct or indirect; (c) The protection of foreign interests in Egypt and the protection of minorities; (d) The Soudan.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence（学术评价）
sources.quote: According to historian Caroline Elkins, the Egyptian independence declaration did not entail sovereignty for Egypt, but rather a "semiautonomous" status.

fact: 图坦卡蒙墓发现后的文物归属争议进入司法程序：卡特在埃及混合法院（Mixed Courts，处理涉及非埃及人纠纷的殖民机构）起诉文物局。1924年3月，麦克斯韦在法庭上称政府「像强盗一样」夺取了陵墓的控制权；混合法院最终判卡特胜诉，但汉纳（Hanna，公共工程部长）把案件上诉到更高法院，该法院于3月31日作出完全支持政府行动的裁决。争议的最终解决方案是：墓中文物不在政府与赞助人之间分配（与此前考古发掘的惯例不同），大部分运往开罗埃及博物馆；卡那封夫人放弃对陪葬品的分配要求，《泰晤士报》的独家报道权终止；卡特于1925年1月25日复工。卡那封的特许权于1929年到期，陵墓所有权归还埃及政府。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
sources.quote: Nevertheless he sued the Antiquities Service in the Mixed Courts of Egypt, a colonial institution for resolving disputes involving non-Egyptians. ... The Mixed Courts ultimately ruled in Carter's favour, but Hanna took the case to a higher court, which on 31 March issued a decision that fully supported his actions. ... Under the agreement that resolved the dispute, the artefacts from the tomb would not be divided between the government and the dig's sponsors, as was standard practice in previous Egyptological digs, and most of the tomb's contents went to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo. ... the Carnarvon concession expired in 1929 and ownership of the tomb reverted to the Egyptian government.

fact: 据一项对埃及工业的统计推算，1922年埃及工业每名从业者的平均净产值为120埃镑；而工人与职员的年平均工资只有30—40埃镑。作者据此推算每名工人平均生产80—90埃镑的剩余价值，剥削率为200%—300%。这组数字是1922年埃及城市雇佣劳动的工资锚点：月均工资约2.5—3.3埃镑。

sources.title: Tony Cliff, Some Features of Capitalist Economy in the Colonies（1947）
sources.quote: According to one calculation the average net income of industry in 1922 was £E120 per man occupied in industry. And seeing that the wages of the workers and officials only came to £E30-40 on an average for the year, we may assume that every worker produced an average surplus value of £E80-90, which gives a rate of exploitation of 200-300 per cent.

fact: 卡特1922—1923年的日记账目记录了发掘队埃及雇员的工资：厨师阿里·阿布·扎伊德自1922年11月21日起的六个月合同为53埃镑，即每月约13埃镑；两名随侍男孩为每月2埃镑；另一名雇员1922年12月27日起五个月合同37.5埃镑，即每月7.5埃镑。同一账目还记有往返开罗与卢克索的运输、汽车与货运开支。

fact: 埃及镑（gineih）于1885年随埃及进入纯金本位而设立，1埃镑含7.4375克纯金，其币值依据英国金索维林的含金量确定。一战爆发、英国中止金本位后，埃及镑采用英镑挂钩：1埃镑兑1英镑6先令（即97.5皮阿斯特兑1英镑），这一汇率维持到1960年代初埃及小幅贬值并转向美元挂钩（1埃镑=2.3美元）为止。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Egyptian pound
sources.quote: In 1885, Egypt went into a purely gold standard, and the Egyptian pound unit, known as the gineih, was introduced at E£1 = 7.4375 grams of fine gold. ... Then, at the outbreak of World War I, with the gold specie standard being suspended in the UK, the Egyptian pound used a sterling peg of one pound and sixpence sterling (£1 0s 6d) to one Egyptian pound. Inverted, this gives E£0.975 for one pound sterling. This exchange value of 97.5 piastres to the pound sterling continued until the early 1960s

fact: 图坦卡蒙墓出土文物编号达5398件。多数运往开罗埃及博物馆，构成该馆常设展品约六分之一；石棺、外层棺与木乃伊留在墓室；最后一批陪葬品于1932年修复完成后运抵开罗。这一体量与运输、修复、编目能力，构成了1920年代埃及文物处理的实际技术边界。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Discovery of the tomb of Tutankhamun
sources.quote: The artefacts from the tomb were numbered at 5,398 distinct objects. ... Most of the remainder were sent to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo, coming to form about a sixth of the museum's permanent exhibits. ... The last of the burial goods were conserved and shipped to Cairo in 1932.

fact: 卢克索的发掘季与旅游季高度重叠：卡特之所以在1922年11月1日提前开工，是为了减少对游客的干扰。这说明帝王谷在1922年已是稳定的冬季旅游目的地，考古作业必须为游客让路——旅游业的季节节律直接决定了发掘的时间表与人力安排。
